author: feral-core
description: Control the local computer: open apps, open web pages in a chosen browser, quit apps, lock the screen, take screenshots, adjust volume, and read system info. Runs one allowlisted program at a time with no shell metacharacters, so it cannot create, read, or edit files. Use coding_tools__write_file / read_file / edit_file / bash for anything touching the filesystem or running a program.

endpoints.description: Open a web page on the user's Mac, optionally in a specific browser. USE THIS FOR ANY REQUEST THAT ENDS AT A WEB PAGE: 'open a YouTube song on Chrome', 'play lofi on YouTube', 'open google.com in Safari', 'pull up the weather'. Runs the allowlisted `open` program (the same program desktop_control__shell_command may run) with the URL as a separate argument and no shell. Do NOT use desktop_control__open_app for this: the natural AppleScript for opening a page is `open location`, which the sandbox policy rejects outright because it dispatches arbitrary URL schemes. Only http:// and https:// URLs are accepted here; file://, javascript:, data:, and application-private schemes are refused. To open a local folder or file instead, use desktop_control__shell_command with `open ~/Downloads`.

params.name: url
params.description: Full http:// or https:// URL. Percent-encode spaces. Query strings with several parameters are fine (&, ?, = all work here, unlike in desktop_control__shell_command). Examples: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=lofi%20hip%20hop, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&t=30s, https://news.ycombinator.com

params.name: app
params.description: Optional browser or app to open the URL in, as its name in /Applications. Omit to use the user's default browser. Omitting it is the right choice unless the user named an app. Examples: Google Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc, Brave Browser.

endpoints.description: Launch or focus an application on the user's Mac with AppleScript. Use for 'open Spotify', 'launch Terminal', 'bring Chrome to the front'. The script parameter is AppleScript, normally `tell application "AppName" to activate`. THE SANDBOX POLICY REJECTS A SCRIPT CONTAINING ANY OF THESE PHRASES, and this is the complete list: `do shell script`, `do script`, `run script`, `load script`, `osascript`, `use framework`, `current application's`, `NSTask`, `system attribute`, `open location`. A script containing one of them returns 403 and nothing runs. In particular `open location` is what you would naturally write to open a web page, and it is denied; call desktop_control__open_url instead. To quit an app use desktop_control__quit_app. To run a program use desktop_control__shell_command.

params.name: script
params.description: AppleScript to execute, normally: tell application "AppName" to activate. Examples: tell application "Music" to activate; tell application "Safari" to activate; tell application "Notes" to activate; tell application "Finder" to activate. Other permitted forms: tell application "System Events" to keystroke "s" using command down; set the clipboard to "some text"; display notification "done" with title "FERAL".

endpoints.description: Quit an application on the user's Mac. Use for 'quit Slack', 'close Spotify', 'shut down Chrome'. The same denied-phrase list as desktop_control__open_app applies (`do shell script`, `do script`, `run script`, `load script`, `osascript`, `use framework`, `current application's`, `NSTask`, `system attribute`, `open location`). An app with unsaved work may show a save dialog and stay open.

params.name: script
params.description: AppleScript to quit one app. MUST use the format: tell application "AppName" to quit. Examples: tell application "Slack" to quit; tell application "Spotify" to quit; tell application "Google Chrome" to quit.

endpoints.description: List the applications currently open on the user's Mac (foreground apps only, not background daemons). Use for 'what apps are running', 'what do I have open'. Requires macOS Accessibility/Automation permission for System Events; if that has not been granted the call returns an authorization error rather than a policy refusal.

params.name: script
params.default: tell application "System Events" to get name of every process whose background only is false
params.description: AppleScript that returns the running app names. The default is correct; leave it alone.

endpoints.description: Lock the user's Mac screen immediately. Use for 'lock my mac', 'lock the screen'. Sends Control-Command-Q through System Events, so macOS Accessibility permission must be granted to the FERAL process; without it the call returns an authorization error. Note that `pmset displaysleepnow` does NOT work here: `pmset` is not on the daemon shell allowlist.

params.name: script
params.default: tell application "System Events" to keystroke "q" using {command down, control down}
params.description: AppleScript that locks the screen. The default is correct; leave it alone.

endpoints.description: Run one allowlisted program on the user's Mac. The command must be a single program from the daemon shell allowlist (open, osascript, screencapture, say, pbcopy, pbpaste, defaults, system_profiler, sw_vers, caffeinate, mdfind, date, uname) with plain arguments. THESE CHARACTERS ARE REJECTED ANYWHERE IN THE COMMAND, quoted or not: $ ` | & ; > < \ and newlines. So pipes, redirects, command substitution and chaining do NOT work, AND a URL containing & (a second query parameter) is refused. Use desktop_control__open_url for URLs. `pbcopy` is on the allowlist but reads its input from stdin, which this path cannot supply; to put text on the clipboard call desktop_control__open_app with `set the clipboard to "text"`. To create or edit a file, use coding_tools__write_file. To run git, tests, or any other program, use coding_tools__bash.

params.name: command
params.description: One allowlisted program with arguments, no metacharacters. Examples: open -a Safari; open ~/Downloads; open /Applications; screencapture -x /tmp/screenshot.png; pbpaste; sw_vers; say "hello"; mdfind kMDItemDisplayName=='notes.txt'; osascript -e 'set volume output volume 40'

endpoints.description: Capture a screenshot of the user's screen to /tmp/feral_screenshot.png. This writes a file and returns the path, it does not return the image; to have the screen described, use screen_capture or gui_computer_use__screenshot, which return the pixels.

params.name: command
params.description: Screenshot command. Must stay a single allowlisted program with no metacharacters.

endpoints.description: Get hardware and OS information for this Mac (model, chip, memory, serial). Use for 'what Mac am I on', 'how much RAM do I have'. For free disk space use desktop_control__disk_space instead.

params.name: command
params.description: System info command. Must stay a single allowlisted program with no metacharacters. Alternatives: sw_vers (OS version only), uname -a.

endpoints.returns_description: {output, exit_code}: the system_profiler hardware report as text

endpoints.description: Report free and total disk space on this Mac. Use for 'how much storage do I have', 'disk space', 'how much space is left'. Note that `df -h` does NOT work here: `df` is not on the daemon shell allowlist; system_profiler is.

params.name: command
params.description: Storage report command. The default is correct; leave it alone.

endpoints.returns_description: {output, exit_code}: free and total capacity per volume

endpoints.description: Set or mute the system output volume on the Mac. Use for 'turn the volume down', 'set volume to 30', 'mute'. Single quotes around the AppleScript, never double quotes: \ is a rejected character on this path.

params.name: command
params.description: osascript command for volume, single-quoted. Examples: osascript -e 'set volume output volume 50'; osascript -e 'set volume output volume 20'; osascript -e 'set volume output muted true'; osascript -e 'set volume output muted false'; osascript -e 'output volume of (get volume settings)' to read the current level.
